findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destinationCalendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` can be `null` or `[]`, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar` becomes `undefined` after destructuring. The following condition dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` unconditionally. Any booking that uses Google Meet but has no destination calendar will throw a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Collective host destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on `null`, so the host calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded. In a collective event where the organizer has no calendar but hosts do, the hosts still do not get calendar invites.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
findings.body: `createEvent` still selects only the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` and ignores the `credentialId` passed by EventManager. For multiple hosts, EventManager calls this once per destination credential, but each call creates the event in the first host's calendar while the booking reference records another host's `externalCalendarId`. This creates events in the wrong calendar and causes later update/delete operations to target a calendar that does not contain the event.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
findings.body: `createEvent` destructures only the first `event.destinationCalendar` entry and uses its `externalId` as the calendar ID. With multiple host destination calendars, every per-host `createEvent` call will attempt to create the event in the first host's calendar, while the resulting booking reference stores the other host's `externalCalendarId`. This breaks multi-host calendar creation and later update/delete for Lark.

findings.title: updateEvent results omit externalId and credentialId required by updateLocation
findings.body: `EventManager.updateLocation` now builds booking references from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent`'s return object does not set either field. Previously those references were populated from `evt.destinationCalendar`. After this change, location updates create booking references with missing `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`, so later updates/cancellations cannot locate the correct calendar event.

findings.title: Organization slug condition was inverted
findings.body: The old code included `slug` on the organization when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` was false via `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. The new code uses `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, so the `slug` is set when billing is enabled and omitted when billing is disabled. This reverses the previous behavior and can break organization creation/subdomain setup depending on the billing flag.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback cannot select a calendar from destinationCalendar array
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is null, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Because the predicate compares against `null`, it never matches. `updateEvent` then passes `undefined` as `calendarId`, causing the update to fail; `deleteEvent` silently falls back to `primary`, which can delete from the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Google organizer email uses first host calendar for all created events
findings.body: For a multi-host collective, each Google credential creates an event on that credential's selected calendar, but the organizer attendee email is always set to `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (the first destination calendar). For the second and subsequent hosts, the organizer email belongs to another user's calendar, which can cause Google Calendar API to reject the insert or record the wrong organizer.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent only filters to the first destination calendar
findings.body: `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` destructures only the first destination calendar and uses its `externalId` to filter `listCalendars` results. With multiple destination calendars/credentials, every per-host creation targets the first host's calendar even though the booking reference records another host's external calendar. Later update/delete can therefore reference a calendar that does not contain the created event.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation branch is duplicated for every calendar reference
findings.body: The new loop over `bookingCalendarReference` still contains the old `allRemainingBookings` recurring deletion block inside it. That block does not use the current `reference`; it iterates all of `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and deletes the first calendar reference of each updated booking. With multiple calendar references, the same deletion operations are scheduled once per reference, and host calendar events that are not in the organizer credentials are not deleted correctly.

findings.title: No test covers multiple host destination calendars
findings.body: Only an existing webhook expectation was changed from `null` to `[]`; there is no automated test that creates a collective event with multiple hosts/calendars and verifies that each host's calendar receives, updates, and cancels the correct event. The core behavior of this PR is currently unverified.
